description:
Moving issues to a terminal state through a filtered bulk update does not promote their now-unblocked dependents to Ready. The single-issue update does. Dependents stay in Backlog with no unmet dependencies and drop out of available-work queries.

## Background

The single-issue update path runs the dependent-readiness cascade after any terminal state change (`crates/jit/src/commands/issue.rs:519-524`, calling `check_auto_transitions` at `issue.rs:804`). The bulk path `apply_bulk_update` (`crates/jit/src/commands/bulk_update.rs:231-282`) publishes each matched issue through `publish_captured_bulk_update` and returns without running that cascade.

Reproduction in a fresh repository:

1. Create issues A and B, and make A depend on B.
2. Bulk-update with filter `state:ready` and target state `done` (matches B only).
3. A stays in `backlog`, reports no unmet dependencies, and is absent from available work.

The same update addressed to B by id moves A to `ready`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: After a bulk update moves issues to Done, every dependent whose dependencies are all terminal is in Ready.
- [hard] REQ-02: After a bulk update moves issues to Rejected, every dependent whose dependencies are all terminal is in Ready.
- [hard] REQ-03: A bulk update that changes no issue to a terminal state leaves dependent states unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-04: Dependent states after a bulk terminal update match those after the same per-issue updates applied by id.
- [hard] REQ-05: A regression test covers a bulk update to a terminal state that unblocks a dependent and asserts the dependent reaches Ready.

## Notes

The cascade can run once after the whole batch rather than once per issue.
title: Bulk state updates to a terminal state leave unblocked dependents in backlog
